([[Flushing, Queens|Flushing, New York]]) | college = * [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]] (2015–2017) * [[Norfolk State Spartans men's basketball|Norfolk State]] (2019–2020) | draft_year = 2020 | career_start = 2020 | years1 = 2020–2021 | team1 = [[Phoenix Hagen]] | years2 = 2021 | team2 = [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]] | years3 = 2021–2023 | team3 = [[KK TFT|TFT]] | years4 = 2023 | team4 = [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] | years5 = 2024 | team5 = [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] | years6 = 2024 | team6 = [[Criollos de Caguas (basketball)|Criollos de Caguas]] | highlights = * [[Macedonian Basketball Cup|Macedonian Cup]] winner (2022) * First-team All-[[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference|MEAC]] (2020) * [[Atlantic 10]] All-Rookie Team (2016) }} '''Jermaine Bishop''' (born February 22, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Norfolk State Spartans men's basketball|Norfolk State Spartans]] and [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis Billikens]]. ==High school career== Jermaine Bishop attended [[Holy Cross High School (Flushing)|Holy Cross High School]] in [[Flushing, Queens|Flushing, New York]]. As a senior in 2014–15, he averaged 20.6 points and 5.3 assists per game while helping the Knights to an appearance in the Catholic High School Athletic Association (CHSAA) AA intersectional semi-finals, the squad's deepest run since 2012. He graduated as Holy Cross' third-leading varsity scorer with 1,375 career points, trailing only [[Sylven Landesberg]] and [[Derrick Chievous]].{{cite web | url=http://www.slubillikens.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=27200&ATCLID=210212706 | title=Jermaine Bishop Bio | work=slubillikens.com | accessdate=March 25, 2016}} ==College career== As a freshman at [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]] in 2015–16, Bishop played in 27 games with 16 starting assignments, averaging 8.9 points, 2.0 rebounds and 2.3 assists in 20.8 minutes per game.{{cite web | url=http://stats.washingtonpost.com/cbk/players.asp?id=131534 | title=#11 Jermaine Bishop | work=WashingtonPost.com | accessdate=March 25, 2016}} A three-time A-10 Rookie of the Week honoree during the 2015–16 season, the first Billiken since 2009 to claim this honor. Bishop led the Billikens in scoring (11.7 ppg) and assists (3.2 apg) in conference games, becoming the first Billiken freshman to lead his team in those categories since SLU joined the A-10 in 2005–06. His free-throw percentage (.864, 51-of-59) was sixth all-time in SLU history and the top mark by a freshman in SLU annals. He recorded three 20-plus games as a freshman, scoring 21 points against [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]] on January 13, a career-high 23 points against [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]] on January 20, and 20 points against [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]] on February 17, a contest where he hit the game-winning basket in overtime.{{cite web | url=http://www.slubillikens.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=27200&ATCLID=210783090 | title=Bishop, Crawford Draw A-10 Honors | work=slubillikens.com | date=March 8, 2016 | accessdate=April 6, 2016}} He subsequently earned A-10 All-Rookie Team honors at the season's end. As a sophomore at [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]] in 2016–17, Bishop played only in 9 games with 9 starting assignments. Nine games into the season, he suffered an ankle injury and was awarded a medical redshirt. At the time of his injury, Bishop was leading the Billikens in scoring and assists, he averaged 11.6 points and 4.7 assists per game. He poured in a career-high 27 points on 11-of-23 shooting (4-of-9 from 3-point range) against [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] in Las Vegas and led the Billikens in scoring against [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] with 11 points and [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] with 12 points.{{Cite news|url=http://www.slubillikens.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=210212706|title=Jermaine Bishop Bio|work=slubillikens.com|access-date=2018-02-26}} As a redshirt sophomore at Saint Louis in 2017–18, Bishop did not compete for personal reasons.{{cite news |last1=Hall |first1=David |title=Norfolk State guard Jermaine Bishop has been on his coach's radar since he was 12. After nearly three years off, he's a star |url=https://www.pilotonline.com/sports/college/norfolk-state/vp-sp-nsu-bishop-011820-20200117-akfwrhqcj5b35egd7b3ymuxsd4-story.html |accessdate=April 1, 2020 |work=[[The Virginian-Pilot]] |date=January 17, 2020}} Bishop transferred to [[Norfolk State University]] for his 2018–19 redshirt junior year. He sat out the season due to NCAA rules as a Division I transfer.{{cite web |last1=Bello |first1=Mike |title=Spartan Basketball Finishes Recruiting Class with Bishop |url=https://nsuspartans.com/news/2018/6/28/mens-basketball-spartan-basketball-finishes-recruiting-class-with-bishop.aspx |website=[[Norfolk State Spartans]] |accessdate=April 1, 2020 |date=June 28, 2018}} In his senior season, he was named to the First Team All-[[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]], the first player for Norfolk since 2017.{{cite press release|url= https://hbcugameday.com/2020/03/06/meac-announces-player-of-the-year-and-postseason-awards/ |title= MEAC announces Player of the Year and postseason awards |publisher=HBCU Gameday |date=March 6, 2020 |accessdate=March 6, 2020}} He also made his way onto the National Association of Basketball Coaches (NABC) All-District 15 second team, and the BOXTOROW HBCU Division I All-America second team. In addition, he earned a spot on the College Sports Information Directors (CoSIDA) Division I Academic All-District 3 team, the first basketball player in NSU history to earn academic all-district accolades. Bishop competed in and started all 31 games; averaged 15.6 points and 3.5 rebounds per game (averaged 18.5 points in MEAC games). For the year, he totaled 483 points, 109 rebounds, 69 assists, 32 steals and four blocks.{{cite news |last1=Gaydos |first1=Ryan |title=2020 Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament: Matchups, players to know & more |url=https://foxwilmington.com/sports/2020-mid-eastern-athletic-conference-mens-basketball-tournament-matchups-players-to-know-more/ |accessdate=April 1, 2020 |work=Fox Wilmington |date=March 10, 2020}} Bishop set the school record for 3-pointers (98) and 3-point attempts (248), breaking the previous marks of 92 (set in 2018–19 and 1986–87) and 237 (set 2007–08), respectively. Ranked first in the MEAC in 3-point field goals (3.2), second in free throw percentage (85.5), fourth in scoring (15.6), fifth in 3-point field goal percentage (39.5), seventh in minutes (33.4), and 15th in assists (2.2). In MEAC games only, led the league in 3-point field goals (3.8) and free throw percentage (87.2) and stood second in scoring (18.5), fourth in 3-point field goal percentage (41.8), ninth in minutes (34.6), and 14th in steals (1.2). Bishop ranked 11th in the nation in 3-point field goals (3.16) and 31st in 3-point field goal percentage. After just one season, he ended the year ranked ninth in NSU career records in 3-point field goal percentage and 19th in 3-pointers.{{Cite web |title=Jermaine Bishop – Men's Basketball |url=https://nsuspartans.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jermaine-bishop/5063 |access-date=June 14, 2026 |website=Norfolk State Spartans Athletics}} He declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=Norfolk State's Jermaine Bishop declares for 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://hbcugameday.com/2020/03/27/norfolk-state-jermaine-bishop-declares-for-2020-nba-draft/ |accessdate=April 8, 2020 |work=HBCU Gameday |date=March 27, 2020}} ==Professional career== On July 21, 2020, Bishop signed with [[Phoenix Hagen]] of the German [[ProA]] league.{{cite news |title=Jermaine Bishop signs with Phoenix Hagen |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jermaine-bishop-signs-with-phoenix-hagen/ |website=Sportando |accessdate=July 21, 2020 |date=July 21, 2020}} On May 28, 2021, Bishop signed with the [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). Bishop was selected by the Indios de Mayagüez in the BSN Draft in the first round with the fourth pick.{{cite web |title=Aleem Ford encabeza selecciones del Sorteo de Nuevo Ingreso 2021 |url=https://www.bsnpr.com/noticias/detalles.asp?r=19364#.YMLixflKi1s/ |website=BSN |accessdate=April 25, 2021 |date=April 25, 2021 |archive-date=April 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426124643/https://www.bsnpr.com/noticias/detalles.asp?r=19364#.YMLixflKi1s/ |url-status=dead }} On December 23, 2021, Bishop signed with the [[KK TFT|TFT]] of both the [[Macedonian First League (basketball)|Macedonian League]] and [[Balkan International Basketball League]] (BIBL).{{cite web |title=Комбо бек што играл во Германија ќе го засили ТФТ |url=https://kos.mk/feniks-ne-go-dava-domashniot-teren/ |website=KOS |accessdate=December 23, 2021 |date=December 23, 2021}} On February 20, 2022, TFT won their first trophy in club history, the [[Cup of Macedonia]], the second most important national basketball title in North Macedonia after the [[Macedonian First League (basketball)]].{{cite web |title=Historical success of TFT, through MZT Skopje to triumph in the Cup |url=https://www.slobodenpecat.mk/en/istoriski-uspeh-na-tft-preku-mzt-skopje-do-triumf-vo-kupot/ |website=Slobodenpecat|accessdate=February 22, 2022 |date=February 22, 2022}} Bishop re-signed with the [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN) for the 2022 season. Due to the extended season with [[KK TFT|TFT]] he only played 9 games. On October 10, 2022, Bishop re-signed with the [[KK TFT|TFT]] of both the [[Macedonian First League (basketball)|Macedonian League]] and [[ABA League Second Division]] (ABA2 League).{{cite web |title=KK TFT Skopje welcomes back Bishop, ex Mayaguez |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/news/771678/KK-TFT-Skopje-welcomes-back-Bishop,-ex-Mayaguez/ |website=LatinBasket |accessdate=October 10, 2022 |date=October 10, 2022}} On February 9, 2023, Bishop was traded from the [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN) to the [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)]].{{cite web |title=TRADE: Jermaine Bishop to Leones de Ponce |url=https://www.bsnpr.com/noticias/cambio-jermaine-bishop-a-los-leones-de-ponce#.ZDBOrXbMK1s/ |website=BSNPR
